10: import type { ThreadMessage, ThreadMessageLike } from "@assistant-ui/react";

12: import type { ChatAttachment, ChatMessage, ChatPart, StudioError } from "../types";
13: import type { UiNode } from "../ui/protocol";
14: 
15: /** The name our generated-surface parts travel under. */
16: export const SURFACE_PART = "odi-surface";
17: 
18: type LikePart = Exclude<ThreadMessageLike["content"], string>[number];
19: 
20: const TOOL_RESULT: Record<string, Record<string, unknown>> = {
21:   ok: { status: "ok" },
22:   error: { status: "error", isError: true },
23:   declined: { status: "declined" },
24: };
25: 
26: function toPart(part: ChatPart): LikePart | null {
27:   switch (part.kind) {
28:     case "text":
29:       return { type: "text", text: part.text };
30: 
31:     case "reasoning":
32:       return { type: "reasoning", text: part.text };
33: 
34:     case "ui":
35:       return { type: `data-${SURFACE_PART}` as const, id: part.id, data: part.node };
36: 
37:     case "source":
38:       return {
39:         type: "source",
40:         sourceType: "document",
41:         id: part.id,
42:         title: part.title,
43:         mediaType: part.mediaType,
44:         ...(part.filename ? { filename: part.filename } : {}),
45:       };
46: 
47:     case "tool": {
48:       const approval = part.approval;
49:       if (approval) {
50:         // A pending write is a question, not a result: the runtime keeps the
51:         // message in `requires-action` until the user answers.
52:         return {
53:           type: "tool-call",
54:           toolCallId: part.id,
55:           toolName: part.name,
56:           args: {},
57:           argsText: "{}",
58:           approval: { id: approval.id, prompt: approval.prompt },
59:         };
60:       }
61:       return {
62:         type: "tool-call",
63:         toolCallId: part.id,
64:         toolName: part.name,
65:         args: {},
66:         argsText: "{}",
67:         result: { ...(TOOL_RESULT[part.status] ?? {}), preview: part.preview ?? "" },
68:         isError: part.status === "error",
69:       };
70:     }
71: 
72:     default:
73:       return null;
74:   }
75: }
76: 
77: function attachmentParts(attachments: ChatAttachment[]) {
78:   return attachments.map((attachment) => ({
79:     id: attachment.id,
80:     type: attachment.contentType.startsWith("image/") ? ("image" as const) : ("document" as const),
81:     name: attachment.name,
82:     contentType: attachment.contentType,
83:     status: { type: "complete" as const },
84:     content: [
85:       {
86:         type: "file" as const,
87:         data: attachment.id,
88:         mimeType: attachment.contentType,
89:         filename: attachment.name,
90:       },
91:     ],
92:   }));
93: }
94: 
95: /**
96:  * A Studio turn as the runtime renders it.
97:  *
98:  * `content` stays the concatenated prose so history replays byte-identically;
99:  * `parts` is what the thread shows.
100:  */
101: export function toThreadMessageLike(message: ChatMessage): ThreadMessageLike {
102:   if (message.role === "notice") {
103:     return {
104:       id: message.id,
105:       role: "system",
106:       content: [{ type: "text", text: message.content }],
107:     };
108:   }
109: 
110:   const parts = (message.parts ?? []).flatMap((part) => {
111:     const converted = toPart(part);
112:     return converted ? [converted] : [];
113:   });
114: 
115:   const content: readonly LikePart[] =
116:     parts.length > 0
117:       ? parts
118:       : message.content
119:         ? [{ type: "text", text: message.content }]
120:         : [];
121: 
122:   const failed = message.error !== undefined;
123: 
124:   return {
125:     id: message.id,
126:     role: message.role,
127:     content,
128:     ...(message.role === "user" && message.attachments?.length
129:       ? { attachments: attachmentParts(message.attachments) }
130:       : {}),
131:     ...(failed
132:       ? {
133:           status: {
134:             type: "incomplete" as const,
135:             reason: "error" as const,
136:             error: message.error as never,
137:           },
138:         }
139:       : {}),
140:     ...(failed || message.retryText
141:       ? {
142:           metadata: {
143:             custom: {
144:               ...(message.error ? { error: message.error } : {}),
145:               ...(message.retryText ? { retryText: message.retryText } : {}),
146:             },
147:           },
148:         }
149:       : {}),
150:   };
151: }
152: 
153: function readCustom(message: ThreadMessage): Record<string, unknown> {
154:   return (message.metadata?.custom ?? {}) as Record<string, unknown>;
155: }
156: 
157: /**
158:  * The inverse: a runtime message back in the Studio's own model.
159:  *
160:  * The runtime hands a branch switch back as the originals it was given, so this
161:  * is only needed when a message arrives from somewhere else — an import, or a
162:  * future remote thread.
163:  */
164: export function toChatMessage(
165:   message: ThreadMessage,
166:   parentId: string | null = null,
167: ): ChatMessage {
168:   const text = message.content
169:     .filter((part) => part.type === "text")
170:     .map((part) => (part as unknown as { text: string }).text)
171:     .join("");
172: 
173:   const custom = readCustom(message);
174:   const parts: ChatPart[] = [];
175: 
176:   for (const part of message.content) {
177:     switch (part.type) {
178:       case "text":
179:         parts.push({ kind: "text", text: part.text });
180:         break;
181: 
182:       case "reasoning":
183:         parts.push({ kind: "reasoning", text: part.text });
184:         break;
185: 
186:       case "source":
187:         parts.push({
188:           kind: "source",
189:           id: part.id,
190:           title: part.sourceType === "url" ? (part.title ?? part.url) : part.title,
191:           mediaType: part.sourceType === "document" ? part.mediaType : "text/html",
192:           ...(part.sourceType === "document" && part.filename
193:             ? { filename: part.filename }
194:             : {}),
195:         });
196:         break;
197: 
198:       case "tool-call": {
199:         const result = part.result as { status?: string; preview?: string } | undefined;
200:         const approval = part.approval;
201:         const awaiting = approval !== undefined && approval.approved === undefined && !part.result;
202:         parts.push({
203:           kind: "tool",
204:           id: part.toolCallId,
205:           name: part.toolName,
206:           status: awaiting
207:             ? "running"
208:             : part.isError
209:               ? "error"
210:               : result?.status === "declined"
211:                 ? "declined"
212:                 : "ok",
213:           ...(result?.preview ? { preview: result.preview } : {}),
214:           ...(awaiting ? { approval: { id: approval.id, prompt: approval.prompt ?? "" } } : {}),
215:         });
216:         break;
217:       }
218: 
219:       case "data":
220:         if (part.name === SURFACE_PART) {
221:           parts.push({
222:             kind: "ui",
223:             id: part.id ?? `ui-${parts.length}`,
224:             node: part.data as UiNode,
225:           });
226:         }
227:         break;
228: 
229:       default:
230:         break;
231:     }
232:   }
233: 
234:   const attachments: ChatAttachment[] | undefined = message.attachments?.length
235:     ? message.attachments.map((attachment) => ({
236:         id: attachment.id,
237:         name: attachment.name,
238:         contentType: attachment.contentType ?? "application/octet-stream",
239:         size: 0,
240:       }))
241:     : undefined;
242: 
243:   const role = message.role === "system" ? "notice" : message.role;
244: 
245:   return {
246:     id: message.id,
247:     parentId,
248:     role,
249:     content: text,
250:     ...(parts.length ? { parts } : {}),
251:     ...(attachments ? { attachments } : {}),
252:     ...(custom.error ? { error: custom.error as StudioError } : {}),
253:     ...(custom.retryText ? { retryText: String(custom.retryText) } : {}),
254:   };
255: }

257: /** The readable text of one appended message, for the Studio's send path. */
258: export function textOf(message: { content: string | readonly { type: string }[] }): string {
259:   if (typeof message.content === "string") {
260:     return message.content.trim();
261:   }
262:   return message.content
263:     .filter((part) => part.type === "text")
264:     .map((part) => (part as unknown as { text: string }).text)
265:     .join("\n")
266:     .trim();

5:  * receives extracted text (or a data URL for an image), never a file handle.

7:  * conversation, and it is silent about failure — a file we cannot read is shown
8:  * as a name, not dressed up as content.
9:  */

12: 
13: import type { ChatAttachment } from "../types";
14: 
15: /** How much of a text file the model sees. */
16: export const MAX_ATTACHMENT_CHARS = 20_000;

18: /** A single image, bounded so a data URL cannot bloat the request. */
19: export const MAX_IMAGE_BYTES = 5 * 1024 * 1024;
20: 
21: export const ATTACHMENT_ACCEPT = [
22:   "text/*",
23:   ".md",
24:   ".mdx",
25:   ".json",
26:   ".csv",
27:   ".yaml",

33:   "image/gif",

38:   ATTACHMENT_ACCEPT.split(",").filter((type) => type.startsWith("image/")),
39: );

799:   /**
800:    * Stream one assistant turn. `base` is the history sent to the model; when
801:    * `userTurn` is given it is appended to that history, otherwise the last
802:    * message of `base` is the turn being re-answered. The new assistant turn is
803:    * parented to `assistantParentId`, which is how branches stay linked.
804:    */
805:   const runTurn = useCallback(
806:     async (
807:       base: ChatMessage[],
808:       userTurn: ChatMessage | null,
809:       assistantParentId: string,
810:     ) => {
811:       if (streaming) {
812:         return;
813:       }
814: 
815:       const history: ChatMessage[] = userTurn ? [...base, userTurn] : base;
816: 
817:       const assistantId = newTurnId();
818:       const assistantIndex = history.length;
819:       setMessages([
820:         ...history,
821:         { role: "assistant", id: assistantId, parentId: assistantParentId, content: "", parts: [] },
822:       ]);
823:       setStreaming(true);
824:       setThinkingPhase("health_check");
825:       setOfflineReply(false);
826: 
827:       const controller = new AbortController();
828:       abortRef.current = controller;
829: 
830:       let content = "";
831:       let parts: ChatPart[] = [];
832:       let steps: RunStep[] = [];
833:       let failure: StudioError | null = null;
834:       let terminal = false;
835:       let stopped = false;
836: 
837:       // Prose is appended to the open text part; a surface opens a new one, so
838:       // the transcript keeps the agent's order instead of gathering all prose
839:       // above all cards.
840:       const appendText = (text: string) => {
841:         if (!text) {
842:           return;
843:         }
844:         content += text;
845:         const last = parts[parts.length - 1];
846:         parts =
847:           last?.kind === "text"
848:             ? [...parts.slice(0, -1), { kind: "text", text: last.text + text }]
849:             : [...parts, { kind: "text", text }];
850:       };
851: 
852:       // The turn owns its own timeline, so a finished run stays inspectable and
853:       // the next turn starts from nothing without a reset elsewhere.
854:       const publish = () => {
855:         setMessages((prev) => {
856:           if (prev.length <= assistantIndex) {
857:             return prev;
858:           }
859:           const next = [...prev];
860:           const retryText = userTurn?.content ?? base[base.length - 1]?.content ?? "";
861:           next[assistantIndex] = {
862:             role: "assistant",
863:             id: assistantId,
864:             parentId: assistantParentId,
865:             content,
866:             parts: [...parts],
867:             ...(failure ? { error: failure, retryText } : {}),
868:             ...(stopped ? { stopped: true, retryText } : {}),
869:             ...(steps.length ? { tools: [...steps] } : {}),
870:           };
871:           return next;
872:         });
873:       };
874: 
875:       const handleEvent = (event: RawSseEvent) => {
876:         switch (event.event) {
877:           case "status": {
878:             const phase = String(event.data.phase ?? "");
879:             setThinkingPhase(phase);
880:             if (phase === "offline") {
881:               setOfflineReply(true);
882:             }
883:             break;
884:           }
885:           case "delta": {
886:             appendText(String(event.data.text ?? ""));
887:             publish();
888:             break;
889:           }
890:           case "ui": {
891:             // Validate again on arrival: the connection is local but the
892:             // renderer must never trust a shape it has not checked.
893:             const parsed = parseUiSpec(event.data.spec, catalogManifest());
894:             if (parsed.ok) {
895:               parts = [
896:                 ...parts,
897:                 { kind: "ui", id: String(event.data.id ?? `ui-${parts.length}`), node: parsed.node },
898:               ];
899:               publish();
900:             }
901:             break;
902:           }
903:           case "tool":
904:             steps = applyToolEvent(
905:               steps,
906:               {
907:                 name: String(event.data.name ?? ""),
908:                 status: String(event.data.status ?? ""),
909:                 preview: event.data.preview ? String(event.data.preview) : undefined,
910:               },
911:               Date.now(),
912:             );
913:             publish();
914:             break;
915:           case "message": {
916:             terminal = true;
917:             content = String(event.data.content ?? content);
918:             const hasSurfaces = parts.some((part) => part.kind === "ui");
919:             if (!hasSurfaces) {
920:               parts = content ? [{ kind: "text", text: content }] : [];
921:             }
922:             publish();
923:             break;
924:           }
925:           case "conversation": {
926:             const id = String(event.data.id ?? "");
927:             if (id) {
928:               setConversationId(id);
929:             }
930:             break;
931:           }
932:           case "memory": {
933:             const observation = event.data.observation as Observation | undefined;
934:             if (observation?.id) {
935:               setMemory((prev) =>
936:                 prev.some((item) => item.id === observation.id)
937:                   ? prev.map((item) => (item.id === observation.id ? observation : item))
938:                   : [...prev, observation],
939:               );
940:             }
941:             break;
942:           }
943:           case "canvas_dirty":
944:             void refreshCanvas();
945:             break;
946:           case "connector": {
947:             if (String(event.data.status ?? "") === "error") {
948:               const reason = String(event.data.error ?? "The connector could not be added.");
949:               setMessages((prev) => [
950:                 ...prev,
951:                 { role: "notice", id: newTurnId(), parentId: null, content: `Connector failed: ${reason}` },
952:               ]);
953:             } else {
954:               setConnectorSuggestions((prev) => {
955:                 const id = String(event.data?.preset ?? event.data?.name ?? "");
956:                 if (!id || prev.includes(id)) {
957:                   return prev;
958:                 }
959:                 return [...prev, id];
960:               });
961:             }
962:             void refreshConnectors();
963:             break;
964:           }
965:           case "error": {
966:             terminal = true;
967:             failure = readStudioError(event.data.error);
968:             publish();
969:             break;
970:           }
971:           default:
972:             break;
973:         }
974:       };
975: 
976:       try {
977:         await streamChat(
978:           {
979:             base_url: settings.base_url,
980:             api_key: settings.api_key,
981:             model: settings.model_name,
982:             mcp_url: settings.mcp_url,
983:             messages: history,
984:             brief,
985:             ui_catalog: catalogManifest(),
986:             conversation_id: conversationId,
987:           },
988:           handleEvent,
989:           controller.signal,
990:         );
991:       } catch (error) {
992:         const aborted = (error as Error).name === "AbortError";
993:         if (aborted) {
994:           // An abort is the user's own doing, so it is not a failure — but it is
995:           // still a fact about the turn. Keep what arrived, stop any tool that
996:           // was mid-flight, and leave the turn in place so the transcript says
997:           // what happened instead of silently losing the question.
998:           stopped = true;
999:           steps = steps.map((step) =>
1000:             step.status === "running"
1001:               ? {
1002:                   ...step,
1003:                   status: "stopped",
1004:                   preview: step.preview ?? "Stopped before it returned.",
1005:                   endedAt: Date.now(),
1006:                 }
1007:               : step,
1008:           );
1009:           publish();
1010:         } else {
1011:           terminal = true;
1012:           failure = asStudioError(error);
1013:           publish();
1014:         }
1015:       } finally {
1016:         if (!terminal && !failure && !stopped) {
1017:           // The stream ended without a message or an error: something failed
1018:           // silently, and the user must still be told.
1019:           failure = {
1020:             code: "internal",
1021:             message: "The assistant stopped before answering.",
1022:             suggestion: "Try again — your question is still here.",
1023:             retryable: true,
1024:           };
1025:           publish();
1026:         }
1027:         setStreaming(false);
1028:         setThinkingPhase(null);
1029:         abortRef.current = null;
1030:       }
1031:     },
1032:     [streaming, settings, brief, conversationId, refreshCanvas, refreshConnectors],
1033:   );

1035:   const sendMessage = useCallback(
1036:     async (
1037:       text: string,
1038:       attachments: ChatAttachment[] = [],
1039:       options: { from?: string } = {},
1040:     ) => {
1041:       const trimmed = text.trim();
1042:       if ((!trimmed && !attachments.length) || streaming) {
1043:         return;
1044:       }
1045: 
1046:       // A re-ask replaces the turn it starts from: the old question and the
1047:       // answer it got are the same turn, and keeping both would read as a
1048:       // conversation the reader never had.
1049:       const cut = options.from
1050:         ? messages.findIndex((message) => message.id === options.from)
1051:         : -1;
1052:       const replaced = cut >= 0 ? messages.slice(0, cut) : messages;
1053: 
1054:       // Files ride only on the newest turn. Re-sending megabytes of base64 with
1055:       // every later question would make each turn slower than the last.
1056:       const history: ChatMessage[] = replaced.map((message) =>
1057:         message.attachments
1058:           ? {
1059:               id: message.id,
1060:               parentId: message.parentId,
1061:               role: message.role,
1062:               content: message.content,
1063:               parts: message.parts,
1064:             }
1065:           : message,
1066:       );
1067:       const userMessage: ChatMessage = {
1068:         id: newTurnId(),
1069:         parentId: history.length ? history[history.length - 1].id : null,
1070:         role: "user",
1071:         content: trimmed,
1072:         ...(attachments.length ? { attachments: attachments as unknown as ChatAttachment[] } : {}),
1073:       };
1074:       await runTurn(history, userMessage, userMessage.id);
1075:     },
1076:     [messages, streaming, runTurn],
1077:   );

1079:   /**
1080:    * Re-answer the turn ending at `messageId`: everything up to and including
1081:    * that message stays, and a new assistant branch grows from it.
1082:    */
1083:   const regenerateFrom = useCallback(
1084:     async (messageId: string | null) => {
1085:       const index = messageId
1086:         ? messages.findIndex((message) => message.id === messageId)
1087:         : messages.length - 1;
1088:       if (index < 0) {
1089:         return;
1090:       }
1091:       const target = messages[index];
1092:       const questionIndex =
1093:         target?.role === "user"
1094:           ? index
1095:           : target?.role === "assistant"
1096:             ? index - 1
1097:             : -1;
1098:       const question = messages[questionIndex];
1099:       if (!question || question.role !== "user") {
1100:         return;
1101:       }
1102:       const base = messages.slice(0, questionIndex + 1);
1103:       await runTurn(base, null, base[base.length - 1].id);
1104:     },
1105:     [messages, streaming, runTurn],
1106:   );

1108:   /**
1109:    * Replace the user turn at `messageId` with edited words, at its original
1110:    * parent, and grow a new assistant branch from it.
1111:    */
1112:   const editFrom = useCallback(
1113:     async (messageId: string | null, text: string, attachments: ChatAttachment[] = []) => {
1114:       const cut = messageId === null ? messages.length - 1 : messages.findIndex((message) => message.id === messageId);
1115:       if (cut < 0 || streaming) {
1116:         return;
1117:       }
1118:       const original = messages[cut];
1119:       const base = messages.slice(0, cut);
1120:       const trimmed = text.trim();
1121:       const edited: ChatMessage = {
1122:         id: original.id,
1123:         parentId: original.parentId ?? null,
1124:         role: "user",
1125:         content: trimmed,
1126:         ...(attachments.length ? { attachments } : { attachments: original.attachments }),
1127:       };
1128:       await runTurn(base, edited, edited.id);
1129:     },
1130:     [messages, streaming, runTurn],
1131:   );

23:

25:   title: string;
26:   label: string;
27:   prompt: string;
28: }
29: 
30: export const OPPORTUNITY_PROMPT =

32: export const FIND_PROMPT =

35:   "I have a bet I'm about to make. Pressure-test it with me: ask what it is, then tell me what would have to be true and what evidence I'm missing.";
36: export const CAPTURE_PROMPT =
37:   "I heard something from a customer that I want to make sense of. Ask me what they said, then help me turn it into something we can act on.";
38: export const FRAME_JOB_PROMPT =
39:   "Help me name the job I'm trying to win. Ask me who it is for and what they are trying to get done.";
40: 
41: /** Starter prompts for the empty state, chosen from what the canvas holds. */
42: export function suggestionsFor(state: {
43:   jobCount: number;
44:   outcomeCount: number;
45: }): StudioSuggestion[] {
46:   return [
47:     {
48:       title: "Sharpen an opportunity",
49:       label: "Turn a hunch into something defensible",
50:       prompt: OPPORTUNITY_PROMPT,
51:     },
52:     state.outcomeCount > 0
53:       ? {
54:           title: "Pressure-test a bet",
55:           label: "Find what would have to be true",
56:           prompt: PRESSURE_TEST_PROMPT,
57:         }
58:       : {
59:           title: "Find the next opportunity",
60:           label: "Look across what you already know",
61:           prompt: FIND_PROMPT,
62:         },
63:     state.jobCount > 0
64:       ? {

67:           prompt: CAPTURE_PROMPT,

77: export function StudioRuntimeProvider({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {
78:   const {
79:     messages,
80:     streaming,
81:     canvas,
82:     sendMessage,
83:     regenerateFrom,
84:     editFrom,
85:     switchBranch,
86:     respondToApproval,
87:     stopStreaming,
88:   } = useStudio();

90:   const attachments = useMemo(() => createAttachmentAdapter(), []);
91:   const jobCount = canvas?.jobs.length ?? 0;
92:   const outcomeCount = canvas?.outcomes.length ?? 0;
93:   const suggestions = useMemo(
94:     () => suggestionsFor({ jobCount, outcomeCount }),
95:     [jobCount, outcomeCount],
96:   );
97: 
98:   const runtime = useExternalStoreRuntime<ChatMessage>({
99:     isRunning: streaming,
100:     messages,
101:     convertMessage: toThreadMessageLike,
102:     suggestions,
103:     adapters: { attachments },
104:     onNew: async (message) => {
105:       await sendMessage(textOf(message), preparedAttachments(message.attachments));
106:     },
107:     onEdit: async (message) => {
108:       await editFrom(message.sourceId, textOf(message), preparedAttachments(message.attachments));
109:     },
110:     onReload: async (parentId, config) => {
111:       await regenerateFrom(config.sourceId ?? parentId);
112:     },
113:     onCancel: async () => {
114:       stopStreaming();
115:     },
116:     setMessages: (next) => {

118:     },
119:     onRespondToToolApproval: async ({ approvalId, approved, reason }) => {
120:       await respondToApproval(approvalId, approved, reason);
121:     },
122:   });

124:   return <AssistantRuntimeProvider runtime={runtime}>{children}</AssistantRuntimeProvider>;

import type { AssistantState } from "./types/client";
import { useAui } from "./useAui";
import { getProxiedAssistantState } from "./utils/proxied-assistant-state";
import { useTrackedSyncExternalStore } from "./utils/scoped-signal";

/**
 * Subscribes to a slice of {@link AssistantState} and re-renders the
 * component whenever that slice changes.
 *
 * The `selector` runs again when a client whose state it read, or a list
 * whose items it looked up, changes; a selector whose reads the store cannot
 * follow, such as one that reads nothing through it, runs on every store
 * update. Its return value is compared by `Object.is`, and the component
 * re-renders only when the selected slice changes. Returning the entire
 * state object is not supported and throws at runtime — select a specific
 * field instead, or compose multiple `useAuiState` calls. Returning a new
 * object or array literal, including spreading `s.thread` into a new object,
 * re-renders the component every time the selector runs; either select
 * primitives or return a memoized reference.
 *
 * Scopes that may be unavailable can be read via `s.optional.<scope>`,
 * which resolves to `undefined` instead of throwing.
 *
 * @param selector - Pure function that derives a value from the current
 *   assistant state. Should be cheap and referentially stable for equal
 *   inputs (plain field reads, primitives, or memoized values).
 * @returns The currently selected slice.
 *
 * @example
 * ```tsx
 * // Disable a button while a run is in flight.
 * const isRunning = useAuiState((s) => s.thread.isRunning);
 * ```
 *
 * @example
 * ```tsx
 * // Prefer multiple selectors over an inline object literal, which would
 * // create a new reference on every render.
 * const text = useAuiState((s) => s.composer.text);
 * const canSend = useAuiState((s) => s.composer.canSend);
 * ```
 */
export const useAuiState = <T>(selector: (state: AssistantState) => T): T => {
  const aui = useAui();
  const proxiedState = getProxiedAssistantState(aui);

  const slice = useTrackedSyncExternalStore(aui.subscribe, () =>
    selector(proxiedState),
  );

  if (
    typeof slice === "object" &&
    slice !== null &&
    ((slice as unknown) === proxiedState ||
      (slice as unknown) === proxiedState.optional)
  ) {
    throw new Error(
      "You tried to return the entire AssistantState. This is not supported due to technical limitations.",
    );
  }

  useDebugValue(slice);

  return slice;
};

/**
 * Subscribes to a slice of {@link AssistantState} and re-renders the
 * component whenever that slice changes.
 *
 * The `selector` runs again when a client whose state it read, or a list
 * whose items it looked up, changes; a selector whose reads the store cannot
 * follow, such as one that reads nothing through it, runs on every store
 * update. Its return value is compared by `Object.is`, and the component
 * re-renders only when the selected slice changes. Returning the entire
 * state object is not supported and throws at runtime — select a specific
 * field instead, or compose multiple `useAuiState` calls. Returning a new
 * object or array literal, including spreading `s.thread` into a new object,
 * re-renders the component every time the selector runs; either select
 * primitives or return a memoized reference.
 *
 * Scopes that may be unavailable can be read via `s.optional.<scope>`,
 * which resolves to `undefined` instead of throwing.
 *
 * @param selector - Pure function that derives a value from the current
 *   assistant state. Should be cheap and referentially stable for equal
 *   inputs (plain field reads, primitives, or memoized values).
 * @returns The currently selected slice.
 *
 * @example
 * ```tsx
 * // Disable a button while a run is in flight.
 * const isRunning = useAuiState((s) => s.thread.isRunning);
 * ```
 *
 * @example
 * ```tsx
 * // Prefer multiple selectors over an inline object literal, which would
 * // create a new reference on every render.
 * const text = useAuiState((s) => s.composer.text);
 * const canSend = useAuiState((s) => s.composer.canSend);
 * ```
 */
export const useAuiState = <T>(selector: (state: AssistantState) => T): T => {
  const aui = useAui();
  const proxiedState = getProxiedAssistantState(aui);

  const slice = useTrackedSyncExternalStore(aui.subscribe, () =>
    selector(proxiedState),
  );

  if (
    typeof slice === "object" &&
    slice !== null &&
    ((slice as unknown) === proxiedState ||
      (slice as unknown) === proxiedState.optional)
  ) {
    throw new Error(
      "You tried to return the entire AssistantState. This is not supported due to technical limitations.",
    );
  }

  useDebugValue(slice);

  return slice;
};
